parts.transcript: S2: radio interview with millionaire Arthur Knowles (plumbing). Mistakes: 'a person who never made a mistake never made anything' - see them as an opportunity to learn (11=A). American studies: too much confidence can reduce chances of success; self-help books a waste (12=A). Studies recommend keeping goals in mind/never give up - remain concentrated on goals (13=C). Marketing: he hired an expert to handle it (14=B). Leadership: be someone your workers look up to - earn respect of the workforce (15=C). Risks: better to tread carefully - advises caution (16=A). Developing the idea, focus on: cater better than existing companies (B) + commit to dedicating ~10 years (C) (17/18=B,C; originality and price rejected). What helped him start: wife's job paid the bills = family support (A) + he could provide a better service than competitors = effective approach (E) (19/20=A,E; recession, unsupportive banks and the advice he was given all rejected).
parts.instruction: You will hear part of a radio programme in which a successful businessman, Arthur Knowles, advises listeners on how to become a self-made millionaire.

parts.transcript: S3: trainee teachers Stefan & Magda on science experiments. Steam engine model - couldn't get it to work, hard to get results = too difficult (21=B). Breakfast cereals taste test - wasn't expensive = cheap to do (22=G). Bouncing balls - improved grasp of charts/graphs/calculation = useful practice for maths (23=F). Making paper from grass - didn't engage/motivate them = very boring (24=A). Tie-dyeing - done over three classes = takes longer than usual (25=H). Glue from milk - got feedback straight away = immediate results (26=E). Condenser diagram (extract plant essences): large outer container made of metal holds hot water = metal container (27=D); a strainer sits inside holding plant matter (rosemary) = integral strainer (28=F); glass container at top holds ice, with a drip tip where essence collects = drip tip (29=G); essence drips into a dish made of pottery at the bottom = pottery container (30=E). (A=glass top, B/C=plant matter piles are distractors.)
parts.instruction: You will hear two primary school trainee teachers called Stefan and Magda discussing their placements for science teaching.

parts.title: Office Design
parts.transcript: S4: talk on research into office/workplace design. Open-plan began early 20th century when businesses needed people (usually women) to do typing (31), sitting in rows. Variations: early designs had separate desks (32); cubicles came with high or low screens (33); now hot-desking means workers share (34) a workstation. Employees dislike open-plan: lack of privacy (35) and security (36, carrying valuables); bad for health (37, borne out by staff records). Employers like it: reduces rent and energy (38) costs; better teamwork; new staff learn by observing so it eases training (39). Reality: unhappy workers distracted by the noise (40) around them.
